newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU calls for security for Zaire aid workers.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for security for Zaire aid workers.

text.p: The European Union's aid chief said Tuesday's African sumit on Zaire must give a clear signal that there will be a ceasefire in eastern Zaire and that corridors to bring aid to refugees will be protected.
European commissioner Emma Bonino, in an interview with the French newspaper Le Figaro published on Tuesday, also called for an early Security Council resolution on protecting humanitarian corridors.
Relief workers as well as refugees needed protection, as they could come under attack from starving mobs who had not had any food for a week, she said.

Leaders of east and central African countries were gathering in Nairobi for talks on the situation in eastern Zaire where more than one million refugees have fled fighting between Zairean forces and Rwanda-backed Tutsi rebels.
Kenya said Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo was staying away.
Bonino called it an unprecedented scandal that relief groups had been prevented from working in the troubled area.

"This is the first time that access was systematically denied to humanitarian (workers), in contempt of international conventions," she said."The real scandal is that everything was there. We have been stopped from supplying water and food to 800,000 people," she said.

Aid workers could resume work rapidly once security was guaranteed. They were at hand, in Nairobi, Kigali and Kampala and there were stockpiles of food and medicine, although these had probably been looted, she said.
Three corridors could be established provided Goma airport was re-opened -- from Uganda to Goma, from Burundi to Uvira, and from Kigali to Gisenyi, she added.

France on Monday proposed to set up a multinational force with the United States, European and African states and Canada to ensure security in eastern Zaire. Washington has said it was studying the proposal but needed clarification of what was involved.
